en: Taal Volcano's main crater sits on an island located inside a lake on the island of Luzon.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River flows directly into the sea, making it one of the few underground rivers affected by ocean tides.
Mount Apo features Lake Venado, which sits at an elevation of 2,840 meters and is the highest lake in the Philippines.
The island province of Camiguin has exactly seven volcanoes, which is more than its five municipalities.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench reaches 10,540 meters, making it the third deepest oceanic trench in the world.
Bohol's famous Chocolate Hills consist of exactly 1,268 cone-shaped mounds that turn cocoa-brown during the dry season.
The Tamaraw, a unique dwarf buffalo, is found exclusively in the mountainous forests of the island of Mindoro.
Lake Mainit in Surigao del Norte reaches a maximum depth of 223 meters, making it the deepest lake in the Philippines.
Callao Cave in Peñablanca, Cagayan, features a naturally illuminated cathedral chamber that locals have converted into an active chapel.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released so much ash that it lowered global temperatures by half a degree.
The northernmost province of Batanes is located just 190 kilometers south of Taiwan, making it the closest Philippine landmass to the island.
The Philippine tarsier, native to islands like Bohol, has eyes that are so large they each weigh more than its entire brain.
